title: A multiplayer movement core
hints: Write the movement function once, outside both classes, and call it from the server's tick, the client's `makeInput` and the client's replay. Prediction is only exact because all three run the very same code.

Keep the server's history as a `std::deque` of (tick, positions of every player). Rewinding to a fractional tick looks up the two whole ticks around it and blends, exactly like the client's interpolation.
On the client, own-player data and other-player data from the same snapshot go to completely different places: one is reconciled, the other is stored for interpolation.
requirements: Movement is identical on server and client, with inputs clamped and positions kept in the arena.
The server ignores old, repeated and excess inputs and applies the rest in order each tick.
With no surprises, prediction makes the client's position follow its inputs exactly, despite latency.
Reconciliation corrects the client after the server changes its position, without losing the inputs still in flight.
Other players are interpolated between snapshots, and out-of-order snapshots are ignored.
Hits are tested against rewound positions, with the rewind limited to 32 ticks, and the nearest player is the one hit.
stretch: Join this with milestone 5: serialise inputs and snapshots into packets, send several recent inputs in every packet so a lost one does not stall the server, and delta-compress snapshots against the last one each client acknowledged (practice 6.02).
